_comment: §9.3 model manifest. JSON, not YAML, on purpose: the acceptance tests (§55.18) load
the shipped artefacts on an interpreter that has no PyYAML, and a manifest that only
the station can read is not a check. load_mapping_document() still accepts .yaml.
This is the Vision 1.0 production baseline (§6): YOLO11n with on-sensor post-processing.
It is a DECLARATION, and §9.3's whole rule is that the declaration is checked against the
device: probe_model() + ModelManifest.require_agreement() at open(), before the first
inference. Values here are what the export is expected to be, not what was measured here.
NOT INSTALLED on this station (rpi-turret, imx500-models 1:1.0.0-1 ships 23 .rpk files,
none of them yolo11n). Install it, or run the offline profile. The adapter refuses to open
a missing model path rather than substituting something else - §9.2.
notes: inference_rate_hz = 16 is §6's expected rate; it sizes §40's per-stage budgets and
§19's frame-interval assumptions. The .rpk reports its own rate, and a mismatch beyond
±35% is reported as a warning at open() - not fatal, because the declared figure is a
nominal capability, but the budgets were derived from it and should be re-derived.
license: unknown to this checkout. Do not ship 'Apache-2.0' because a sibling model
carried that; verify the artefact's own licence and fill this in.
bbox_normalized: true means the on-sensor post-processor emits fractions of the network
input. Read those four numbers as pixels instead and every box is wrong by 640x - which
is why the flag is declared, checked, and re-checked at open() (§14).
labels are declared as the 80-entry contiguous COCO list only because the artefact is
not installed to inspect. The installed imx500-models detectors emit a 90-entry list
with '-' placeholders (coco_rpk); when this .rpk arrives, read its embedded metadata
(or run --probe-model --emit-manifest) and correct this file from the answer.
